text: So we are a frontier research and product team that combines startup speed with the scale and the resources of Amazon.

text: And we are really focused on building knowledge work agents that can perceive, reason, and act in a variety of different environments to complete real-world tasks.

text: So I want to share a bit about our approach and how we think about agents.
speaker: SPEAKER_05

text: Across three different ways.
speaker: SPEAKER_05

text: So the first is around collaboration.
speaker: SPEAKER_05

text: So we really think about building agents that are teammates much more than just a black box.
speaker: SPEAKER_05

text: And when we say teammates, we really want an agent that can understand what our goal is, our objective is, and can share how they're thinking about achieving that goal.
speaker: SPEAKER_05

text: And then...
speaker: SPEAKER_05

text: Grounding all of that in actual customer use cases.
speaker: SPEAKER_05

text: And so we work very, very closely with a large number of customers to really help ground all the work that we're doing with agents.
speaker: SPEAKER_05

text: And the second is around perception.
speaker: SPEAKER_05

text: So agents need to understand their environment.
speaker: SPEAKER_05

text: And so for us, because it's a perception-based agent, the environment spans multiple devices.
speaker: SPEAKER_05

text: So we started with browsers last year, but you can imagine any visual screen is an environment for our agent to carry out knowledge work in.
speaker: SPEAKER_05

text: So mobile devices and also computer use is the other one.
speaker: SPEAKER_05

text: And the third one is reliability.
speaker: SPEAKER_05

text: And we have a great customer quote that said, if my agent works 50% of the time, it doesn't work at all.
speaker: SPEAKER_05

text: And that's because you're either not going to run it at all, or if you do run it, you're going to end up debugging it and spending all this time, and you're going to basically do away with all the gains that you're getting from that agent.

text: And so we spend a lot of time building and training our models in simulated environments for reinforcement learning.

text: So, for those of you who are not familiar with the term of computer use, that's basically the way for an agent to take an action on a computer screen, right?
speaker: SPEAKER_05

text: So you see a blue button in the right corner, and you tell your agent, hey, go click this blue button over here.
speaker: SPEAKER_05

text: Very important, very powerful.
speaker: SPEAKER_05

text: It's very important for automating workflows.
speaker: SPEAKER_05

text: But we feel that there's another half of that, which is the agent actually understanding what it's seeing on the screen itself.
speaker: SPEAKER_05

text: Not just using that as a sort of blind screen that it can just go and click on elements there.

text: So if I...

speaker: SPEAKER_05

text: And the second one is these agents don't require APIs in order to work.

text: So if you think about a lot of knowledge work, it's a lot of humans using screens that just don't have APIs, and that's why there are people who are doing these things.
